new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the (open-syllable, mostly disyllabic) word; it is non-contrastive, and when suffixes are added the stress moves rightward so as to stay on the new penult. The statement is made for every present-day Bungku-Tolaki language, of which Kodeoha (KOD) is one of the 15 named, with Mead's Kodeoha data coming from his own 1988 field notes. Mead 1999 App. 3 (p.101) applies the same default to the Kodeoha word lists: unmarked forms are to be read with penultimate stress on the next-to-last written vowel, and none of the 76 KOD rows carries a stress mark.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Kodeoha. Fn.4 (p.16): phonetically long vowels (analysed as two like vowels, argued from stress placement); Mead 1999 p.102 notes compensatory vowel lengthening in Kodeoha (ko:bera 'machete') after the merger of prenasalised and voiced stops, and that a prestress lengthened vowel may reflect a pronunciation midway between a VV sequence and a single vowel.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (roots and suffixed words; 'suffixation usually precipitating stress movement'). Family-wide generalisation over all 15 Bungku-Tolaki languages, not a Kodeoha-specific phonology; no Kodeoha examples with stress marks are given.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement is Mead's family-wide generalisation over all present-day Bungku-Tolaki languages (Mead 1998 pp.16, 97), which explicitly include Kodeoha (KOD, kode1237, ISO vko; alternate names Kondeha, Kondea; 'DIALECTS: none' per Mead 1999 p.78); Mead's Kodeoha data are his own 1988 field notes and word lists 112-113 (Awo, Malamala, Lasusua). No Kodeoha-specific phonology exists (Mead 1999 p.103; Glottolog desc refs = 0; OLAC lists only the 1995 wordlist volume).

sources.note: p.16 sec.1.5 (Kodeoha entry heads the same page; 'Data on Kulisusu and Kodeoha consonants have been drawn from my own field notes'): 'Stress is penultimate (non-phonemic), with suffixation usually precipitating stress movement.' p.97 sec.3.1.2: 'All present-day Bungku-Tolaki languages also exhibit penultimate stress.' Sec.1.5.3 Kodeoha (p.19) = consonant inventory only. Fn.4 p.16: phonetically long vowels are sequences of two like vowels, argued 'from patterns of stress placement'. Both stress sentences verified on the page images.

sources.note: Kodeoha entry (sec.3.4.3, pp.77-78) is lexicostatistic/sociolinguistic; only phonological note is the loss of prenasalised stops. App.3 p.101 convention (g): 'In the absence of any stress marking, one can assume penultimate stress occurring on the next to last written vowel.'; p.102 (d) no phonemic long vowels, Kodeoha ko:bera 'machete' = compensatory lengthening. 76 KOD (Kodeoha, lists 112-113, Awo and Malamala, Lasusua, Aug 1988) rows in App.3 carry no stress marks. p.103: no phonological description exists for Kodeoha (only Tolaki, Padoe, Mori, Moronene).
